mainTopic: A ברייתא about פיגול in the inner sprinklings challenges ריש לקיש's 'first intent' explanation of רבי מאיר. Several answers follow, ending with רבא and רב אשי.
overview: Just before this amud, the גמרא brought two explanations of רבי מאיר's view that an offering becomes פיגול even when the bad intent was in only part of the מתיר. רבי יוחנן says half a מתיר is enough. ריש לקיש says a person keeps acting on his first intent. The גמרא now quotes a ברייתא about the blood sprinklings inside the היכל. There, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול even if the bad intent came in the second or third set, and that seems to go against ריש לקיש. רב יצחק בר אבין answers that the case is a new שחיטה, which is a complete מתיר. רבא explains that the חכמים who disagree follow רבי אליעזר, who requires the whole act. But רבא himself taught that רבי אליעזר agrees that with blood a partial service counts, so this answer falls. רבא then reads the ברייתא as bad intent in the first set, silence in the second, and bad intent again in the third. רב אשי objects that the ברייתא never says 'silent'. He reads it as bad intent in the first three sets and silence in the fourth, teaching that the first intent carries through every set.

steps.title: The ברייתא about פיגול in the inner sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא (quoted as a challenge) teaches that for blood placed on the inner altar, רבי מאיר says bad intent in any one set of sprinklings makes it פיגול with כרת. The חכמים require the bad intent during the entire מתיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for blood that goes on the inner altar, like the 43 sprinklings of יום הכיפורים, the 11 of the פר כהן משיח, and the 11 of the פר העלם דבר של ציבור: if he had a פיגול intent in the first, second, or third set, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול and there is כרת. The חכמים say there is no כרת unless the intent was during the whole מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a ברייתא about the inside blood offerings. It is setting this up as a challenge to ריש לקיש, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These inside offerings have several sets of sprinklings, and all of them together make up the מתיר. רבי מאיר says bad intent in any single set is enough for פיגול. The חכמים say it must cover the whole מתיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner (golden) altar inside the היכל
The bull brought by the כהן גדול for a sin done by mistake
The bull brought when the community sins by mistake because of a wrong ruling of the בית דין
An offering ruined by the intent to eat it or offer it after its proper time
Spiritual 'cutting off', the punishment for eating פיגול
The act that makes an offering permitted, such as the placing of the blood

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'first, second, third' does not mean three separate offerings. It means three sets of sprinklings that all belong to the same offering.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דָּמִים הַנִּיתָּנִין עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי –
phrases.english: But blood that is placed on the inner altar,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן אַרְבָּעִים וְשָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: such as the forty-three of Yom Kippur,
phrases.notes: Forty-three sprinklings in all, from the bull and the goat of יום הכיפורים.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַד עָשָׂר שֶׁל פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ,
phrases.english: and the eleven of the bull of the anointed priest,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַד עָשָׂר שֶׁל פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִיבּוּר;
phrases.english: and the eleven of the bull for a hidden matter of the community;
if he made it piggul whether in the first
or in the second or in the third,
phrases.notes: First, second, third here means the sets of sprinklings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: it is piggul,
and one is liable to karet for it;
and the Sages say: there is no karet for it
unless he makes piggul during the entire permitting factor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל דָּמִים הַנִּיתָּנִין עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting before this section, as a challenge to ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: bad intent in any one set of inner sprinklings makes the offering פיגול with כרת. חכמים: there is no כרת unless the bad intent covered the whole מתיר.

steps.title: Bad intent even in a later set goes against ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says רבי מאיר holds it is פיגול even if the bad intent came only in the second or third set. That does not fit ריש לקיש's 'first intent' reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyway, it teaches that he made it פיגול in the first, second, or third set, and still רבי מאיר disagrees with the חכמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the ברייתא to attack ריש לקיש's explanation of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said רבי מאיר's reason is that a person keeps acting on his first intent, so the bad intent has to be at the start. But here bad intent in only the second or third set is also enough. That sounds like רבי יוחנן's idea that bad intent in half a מתיר works.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In any case, it teaches', pointing to the part of a source that matters for the argument
He disagrees

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
he made it piggul whether in the first
whether in the second, whether in the third,
and he disagrees!
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי מאיר, who still says it is פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's explanation that רבי מאיר's reason is 'a person acts on his first intent'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If bad intent in a later set alone makes it פיגול, the reason cannot be the first intent. It must be that bad intent in half a מתיר is enough.

steps.title: The case is bad intent during a new שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבין explains that the ברייתא is talking about bad intent during שחיטה. A שחיטה is a complete מתיר by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבין said: Here we are dealing with a case where the bad intent was during the שחיטה, which is one whole מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by moving the case of the ברייתא from the sprinklings to the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the blood spilled after one set of sprinklings, so a new animal had to be slaughtered for the next set. The bad intent was during that new שחיטה, which is a whole מתיר on its own. So רבי מאיר's ruling here has nothing to do with 'half a מתיר'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What are we dealing with here?', the opening for narrowing a case
Slaughtering the offering
One complete permitting factor

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avin said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
A case where he made it piggul during slaughter,
which is one permitting factor.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about bad intent during one of the sets of sprinklings, which would be half a מתיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bad intent was during a new שחיטה, which is a complete מתיר, so ריש לקיש's view survives.

steps.title: Then why do the חכמים disagree?
steps.stepSummary: If the bad intent was during a full מתיר (the שחיטה), why would the חכמים say there is no כרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the case is a complete שחיטה, the חכמים's disagreement seems hard to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that bad intent during a complete מתיר makes an offering פיגול. So once the case is a full שחיטה, the חכמים should agree with רבי מאיר. Their disagreement now needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What is the reason of the חכמים?

phrases.english: If so, what is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בר אבין's reading that the case is a full שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bad intent during a whole מתיר makes it פיגול by everyone's view. So the חכמים's disagreement makes no sense in this case.

steps.title: The חכמים here are רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the חכמים in this ברייתא hold like רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who are these חכמים? It is רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by naming whose view the חכמים are following. He brings the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the חכמים's view here belongs to רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר holds that a person is not liable until the whole required item or act is done. So here, every one of the שחיטות would need bad intent.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who are the חכמים?', identifying who stands behind an unnamed view

phrases.english: Rava said: Who are the Sages?
It is Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Naming the source of the view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים's disagreement has no reason once the case is a full שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים follow רבי אליעזר, who requires the whole thing to be done before there is liability.

steps.title: Proof: רבי אליעזר requires the whole amount offered outside
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that offering a כזית of a קומץ, לבונה, קטורת, or certain מנחות outside the Temple makes a person liable. רבי אליעזר exempts him until he offers all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: the קומץ, the לבונה, the קטורת, the מנחת כהנים, the מנחת כהן משיח, and the מנחת נסכים. If someone offered a כזית of one of them outside, he is liable. רבי אליעזר exempts him until he offers all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show that רבי אליעזר requires the complete act, not just part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ת״ק says that offering even a כזית outside counts. רבי אליעזר says there is no liability until the whole item is offered. In the same way, the חכמים in our ברייתא would want bad intent in every one of the שחיטות.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה to be burned on the altar
Frankincense
The incense
The flour offering that comes along with the wine libations of an animal offering
The size of an olive, the usual minimum amount
Outside the Temple, which is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: For now, רב יצחק בר אבין and רבא defend ריש לקיש this way: the ברייתא is about a new, complete שחיטה, and the חכמים follow רבי אליעזר. But this answer does not hold. Step 7 challenges it, and in step 8 רבא drops it with 'אֶלָּא'.

phrases.english: As we learned: The handful, and the frankincense, and the incense,
and the meal offering of priests, and the meal offering of the anointed priest,
and the meal offering of libations;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִקְרִיב מֵאַחַת מֵהֶן כְּזַיִת בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: if he offered an olive-bulk from one of them outside, he is liable.
And Rabbi Eliezer exempts him,
unless he offers all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבא's claim in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר requires the complete act before there is liability
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about offering a כזית of the קומץ and similar items outside the Temple

steps.title: רבא himself said רבי אליעזר agrees about blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer from step 5. רבא himself taught that רבי אליעזר agrees that with blood, even part of the service counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say that רבי אליעזר agrees when it comes to blood? We learned in a משנה that רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון say: from the place where he stopped, there he starts again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer that the חכמים hold like רבי אליעזר. It uses רבא's own statement that רבי אליעזר treats blood differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's 'only a full act counts' rule works for things like a קומץ. But with blood he holds that each sprinkling counts on its own. The proof is that if the blood spills in the middle, the כהן picks up from where he stopped. So רבי אליעזר's view cannot explain why the חכמים say there is no כרת for blood.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (admits a point)
Blood of the offerings
From the place where he stopped
He starts (again)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is arguing with someone else here. The question uses רבא's OWN earlier statement against his own answer.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
And Rabbi Eliezer agrees regarding blood
as we learned in a משנה:
Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Shimon say:
From the place where he stopped,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in יומא about יום כיפור blood that spilled partway through the sprinklings.

phrases.english: from there he begins again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 5, which was backed up in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that the חכמים of the ברייתא follow רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר agrees that a partial blood service counts. So his view cannot explain why the חכמים say there is no כרת when bad intent came in only some of the blood sprinklings.

steps.title: רבא's new case: bad intent, then silence, then bad intent again
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops his first answer. He explains the ברייתא as a case of פיגול intent in the first set, silence in the second, and פיגול intent again in the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The case is where he had פיגול intent in the first set, was silent in the second, and then had פיגול intent again in the third.
steps.whatsHappening: After the challenge in step 7, the 'new שחיטה' approach is dropped. רבא gives a brand-new reading of the ברייתא about the sprinklings themselves that fits ריש לקיש. The ברייתא does not mean 'first OR second OR third'. It describes one specific pattern of intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the bad intent really did start in the first set, just as ריש לקיש requires. The second and third sets just add details. The next step explains what this case is meant to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent (had no stated intent)
And he went back (did it again)
He had an intent that makes the offering פיגול

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
For example, where he had a פיגול intent during the first set,
and was silent during the second,
and again had a פיגול intent during the third.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge in step 7, רבא drops both the 'new שחיטה' reading (step 3) and the רבי אליעזר answer (step 5). He gives a new explanation of the ברייתא that fits ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא meant bad intent in any one of the sets, even if it was only the second or the third.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means bad intent in the first set, silence in the second, and bad intent again in the third.

steps.title: What רבא's case comes to teach
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the new point. Even though he repeated the bad intent in the third set, his silence in the second set still counts as continuing his first intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: if he really continues with his first intent, why did he need to say the פיגול intent again in the third set? So the ברייתא teaches us that he does continue with his first intent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is finishing his answer by explaining why the ברייתא needed to teach this case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person might reason that repeating the intent in the third set shows he did NOT have it in mind during the second set. The ברייתא rejects that reasoning. The silent second set still carries his first intent.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken idea)
With the first intent
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: bad intent, then silence, then bad intent again. The silent set still counts as being done with the first intent.

phrases.english: You might have said:
If it enters your mind
that he continues with his first intent,
why do I need him to have a פיגול intent in the third?
It teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the new teaching behind רבא's case in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the new point of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating the intent in the third set shows he did not have it in mind during the second set.
steps.terutzMaskana: His silence in the second set still continues his first intent.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא never says he was silent
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects. The ברייתא never mentions silence, even though silence is the key detail of רבא's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenges it: Does the ברייתא say 'he was silent'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רבא's new reading because it does not match the words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If silence in the second set were the whole point, the ברייתא would have said so. Since it does not, רבא's reading adds something that is not in the text.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it
Does it teach that? (It does not)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi challenges it:
Does it teach "he was silent"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading from steps 8 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's case of silence in the second set
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The main detail of the case, silence, is missing from the words of the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב אשי's case: bad intent in the first three sets
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the ברייתא as a case of פיגול intent in the first, second and third sets. He was silent only in the fourth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: What case are we dealing with? Where he had פיגול intent in the first set, in the second, and in the third.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own reading of the ברייתא. It fits the words better, because the ברייתא does list the first, second and third sets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's list becomes 'and', not 'or'. He had the bad intent in all three sets, and it started in the first set, as ריש לקיש requires. The next step explains what this case teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
The third (set of sprinklings)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
What are we dealing with here?
For example, where he had a פיגול intent during the first set,
and during the second, and during the third.
phrases.notes: In this case he says nothing during the fourth and last set of sprinklings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's case after the objection in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bad intent, then silence, then bad intent again (רבא).
steps.terutzMaskana: Bad intent in the first, second and third sets, with silence in the fourth.

steps.title: What רב אשי's case comes to teach
steps.stepSummary: Even though he repeated the bad intent in every set, the ברייתא teaches that he is still treated as acting with his first intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: if anyone who acts does so with his first intent, why did he need to repeat the פיגול intent in each and every set? So the ברייתא teaches us that he still acts with his first intent, even in the silent fourth set.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his answer by explaining the new point of his case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person might think that repeating the intent each time shows it does not carry over on its own. Then the silent fourth set would have no bad intent. The ברייתא teaches that the first intent still carries through all the sprinklings.

keyTerms.meaning: Anyone who does (an act)
Each and every one

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבא and רב אשי read the ברייתא using the rule 'anyone who acts does so with his first intent'. They only argue about which case the ברייתא describes.

phrases.english: You might have said:
If it enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה עַל דַּעַת רִאשׁוֹנָה הוּא עוֹשֶׂה –
phrases.english: that anyone who does an act does it with his first intent,
then to again have a פיגול intent
in each and every set, why do I need it?
It teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the new teaching behind רב אשי's case in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the new point of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating the intent in every set shows the first intent does not carry over on its own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first intent still carries over to every later act, including the silent fourth set.
